geo_config._doc: Geography verdict = national sector score plus a capped state adjustment: (state local score - 50)/50 x local_adj_max_points, so at most +/-10 points. The state adjustment alone can never push a sector that is not Avoid nationally into Avoid. Ground-check ratings can only pull a call toward Caution.

combos.label: Caution
combos.message: Caution: national 61 -10 state adjustment (capped at +/-10) = 51.

brief.local_flavour: Limited local coverage. With no recent local articles, the verified figures carry the picture: Jammu and Kashmir GST collections are -10.6% Apr-to-date versus India +6.1%, and the latest month is -29.4% YoY, pointing to shrinking taxable turnover and thinner cash flow across local borrowers. Electricity demand is -0.5% Apr-to-date against India +9.5%, though the latest month rebounded +6.4% YoY, so power-linked operating costs and billing arrears need checking. All-bank credit stands at Rs 116,297 Cr, +11.2% YoY, with a credit-deposit ratio of 56.9%, meaning borrowing is still growing into a softer revenue base. For repayment, the gap between credit growth and falling GST turnover is the key risk: service capacity depends on collections recovering, not on new lending.

brief.local_flavour: Limited local coverage. The only local item is a reference page on the Chandigarh (UT) MSE Facilitation Council, which handles delayed-payment claims from Udyam-registered micro and small suppliers; it aims to decide within 90 days and awards interest at three times the RBI bank rate, with appeals requiring a 75% deposit. That matters because Chandigarh GST collections rose 3.4% Apr-to-date versus India’s 6.1%, and electricity demand rose 3.9% versus 9.5%, so cash generation is softer than the national run-rate even as all-bank credit is Rs 94,919 Cr, up 9.6% YoY, with a 71.9% credit-deposit ratio. For borrowers, slower turnover plus unpaid invoices can stretch repayment; the Council route is a recovery lever, not a substitute for checking debtor days.

That matters because Chandigarh GST collections rose 3.4% Apr-to-date versus India’s 6.1%, and electricity demand rose 3.9% versus 9.5%, so cash generation is softer than the national run-rate even as all-bank credit is Rs 94,919 Cr, up 9.6% YoY, with a 71.9% credit-deposit ratio. For borrowers, slower turnover plus unpaid invoices can stretch repayment; the Council route is a recovery lever, not a substitute for checking debtor days.
borrower_checks: Debtor days: receivables divided by average daily sales; benchmark 90 days or lower
GST turnover vs bank credit summations: compare annual GSTR-3B turnover with bank credit summations; benchmark GST turnover at least 1.2x credit summations
Electricity bills trend vs last year: compare latest quarter billed units with the same quarter last year; benchmark no decline greater than 10%
brief.change_the_call: The call is OK to lend at or above 65; it changes to Caution between 45 and 64 and to Avoid below 45, so a score falling below 65 is the move that changes the call.

local_view.why: Chandigarh GST and electricity growth lag India, and delayed-payment claims signal cash-flow strain.

brief.local_flavour: Limited local coverage beyond a single event: a three-day electricity employees' strike in October 2026, reported by ETV Bharat, The Hindu and Times of India, which shut units in Gurugram, Faridabad, Karnal, Ambala, Panipat and Bahadurgarh. brief.local_flavour: Limited local coverage. But electricity demand is -0.6% Apr-to-date against India +9.5%, and -1.7% YoY in the latest month, which points to softer actual operating activity than the tax line suggests. All-bank credit is Rs 10,653 Cr, +17.4% YoY, with a credit-deposit ratio of 31.0%, so borrowing is expanding faster than the deposit base. For borrowers, the gap between rising GST and falling power use means repayment capacity depends on collections, not billed turnover; slower activity can stretch debtor days and delay payments.

But electricity demand grew only 6.0% Apr-to-date against India's 9.5%, and 5.4% in the latest month, so output-side momentum is softer than the tax line suggests. All-bank credit stands at Rs 4,483,171 Cr, +11.2% YoY, with a credit-deposit ratio of 98.1%, meaning funding is already stretched. For borrowers, the gap between firm GST turnover and weak power draw implies inventory and receivable build-up; repayment capacity depends on converting that turnover to cash rather than on new borrowing.

brief.local_flavour: Limited local coverage. The freshest local signal is a cost shock rather than a demand shock: KASSIA has threatened a shutdown over a power tariff hike of Rs 2.89 per unit, and the CM has ruled out a cut for industries while attributing heavy bills to arrears of the last two months (news). That sits against a strong demand backdrop in the data pack, with Karnataka electricity demand up 23.3% Apr-to-date versus India's 9.5% and GST collections up 11.1% versus 6.1% nationally. For borrowers, higher unit power charges and arrears-loaded bills compress operating cash flow at the same time as all-bank credit of Rs 1,371,514 Cr grows 10.7% YoY, so repayment capacity depends on whether turnover growth outpaces the energy bill.
borrower_checks: GST turnover growth versus growth in bank credit summations, using the state benchmark of +11.1% GST Apr-to-date as the reference line

Electricity cost per unit and monthly bill trend versus last year, checking whether arrears of prior months are embedded in the current bill
brief.change_the_call: A score falling below 65 would move the call from OK to lend to Caution; a score below 45 would move it to Avoid.

brief.local_flavour: Limited local coverage. Tiruppur's knitwear cluster dominates the local news: the All Entrepreneurs Federation says input and dyeing costs have risen over 50 percent, more than 50 percent of units have already closed, and the remaining firms face labour shortage and an indirect power tariff increase, with a protest planned after Nov 10 (news). That squeezes borrower cash flow directly, since 90 percent of these firms are MSMEs employing about 10 lakh workers (news). Statewide, GST collections fell 3.2 percent Apr-to-date against India's +6.1 percent, and the latest month was down 4.5 percent YoY, while electricity demand rose 12.2 percent YoY in the latest month. Falling tax receipts with rising power draw point to thinner turnover and higher running costs, so repayment capacity is weakening even as all-bank credit stands at Rs 1,762,746 Cr, +11.4 percent YoY.
borrower_checks: GST turnover trend vs bank credit summations: monthly GST-reported sales should reconcile to credit-account credits within 10 percent
Debtor days vs 90, with ageing split for receivables over 90 days
Electricity bills trend vs last year: latest month units and tariff per unit compared with the same month a year earlier
brief.change_the_call: A score falling below the OK threshold of 65 would move the call from OK to lend to Caution; a score below the Avoid threshold of 45 would make it Avoid.

local_view.why: GST down 3.2 percent while power demand up 12.2 percent; Tiruppur closures.

brief.local_flavour: Limited local coverage. With no recent local articles, the read rests on the data pack. Puducherry GST collections are -20.7% Apr-to-date against India +6.1%, and the latest month is -30.9% YoY, while electricity demand is +6.1% Apr-to-date versus India +9.5%. Weak tax collections point to softer turnover and thinner cash buffers for local borrowers, so repayment capacity depends more on receivables than on sales growth. All-bank credit of Rs 24,561 Cr, +12.1% YoY, with a credit-deposit ratio of 72.0%, shows borrowing still expanding into a shrinking tax base, which raises the risk that working-capital lines fund unpaid bills rather than output.

brief.local_flavour: Limited local coverage. Tiruppur's knitwear cluster dominates the local news: the All Entrepreneurs Federation says input and dyeing costs have risen over 50 percent, more than 50 percent of units have already closed, and the remaining firms face labour shortage and an indirect power tariff increase, with a protest planned after Nov 10 (news). That squeezes borrower cash flow directly, since 90 percent of these firms are MSMEs employing about 10 lakh workers (news). Statewide, GST collections fell 3.2 percent Apr-to-date against India's +6.1 percent, and the latest month was down 4.5 percent YoY, while electricity demand rose 12.2 percent YoY in the latest month. Falling tax receipts with rising power draw point to thinner turnover and higher running costs, so repayment capacity is weakening even as all-bank credit stands at Rs 1,762,746 Cr, +11.4 percent YoY.
